rfi.title: Whistleblowing is on the rise in France, but expert says support remains lacking
rfi.description: Whistleblowing in France is on the rise, according to the independent authority in charge of protecting those who speak out in the public interest. The Défenseur des Droits has seen an increase in cases, reflecting a growing awareness of the process of speaking out and the protection available for those who do.

rfi.title: Armenia election result revives hopes of reopening border with Turkey
rfi.description: Nikol Pashinyan’s sweeping re-election in Armenia has raised fresh hopes that the border with Turkey could finally reopen after three decades of closure. The Armenian prime minister campaigned on restoring ties with Turkey and Azerbaijan, as well as moving Armenia closer to Europe – but constitutional reform remains a major obstacle.

rfi.title: Resumption of $20bn Cabo Delgado gas project reignites both hope and resentment
rfi.description: The resumption of one of the world's biggest gas projects by French energy giant TotalEnergies, after a five-year suspension following a deadly jihadist attack, has raised hopes of jobs and prosperity in northern Mozambique. But this second instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – questions whether the country's vast gas wealth will benefit local communities.

rfi.title: Paris no longer carries the load as audit backs asylum redistribution plan
rfi.description: France's system for moving asylum seekers from the Paris region to other parts of the country has helped ease pressure on accommodation, but is not being used to its full potential and remains unevenly applied, according to the country's public spending watchdog.

rfi.title: What's in the landmark EU migration reform hardening border protections?
rfi.description: A major reform of European migration rules aimed at hardening border procedures and overhauling the asylum process comes into force on Friday.

rfi.title: Israeli and Palestinian groups urge action on two-state solution in Paris
rfi.description: Israeli and Palestinian civil society groups will meet in Paris on Friday to urge the international community not to abandon a two-state solution, as France seeks to keep the issue on the agenda amid the ongoing war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Sudan rights groups blame RSF paramilitary for drone strikes that hit civilians
rfi.description: Drone strikes blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have killed at least 23 civilians and wounded 19 others in the Sudanese city of El-Obeid, local monitoring groups have said, as the use of armed drones continues to spread across the country in its more than three-year war.

rfi.title: British art 'giant' David Hockney dies aged 88
rfi.description: British artist David Hockney, one of the most influential and defining figures in contemporary art, whose paintings captured the world in brilliant colour, has died aged 88, his publicist announced Friday.

rfi.title: Two French cities impose curfews for under-16s during World Cup
rfi.description: The mayors of Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand are imposing nighttime curfews on children under 16 during the 2026 World Cup. They say the move is aimed at preventing the violent unrest seen after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory last month.

rfi.title: Rise in adulterated cannabis in France, as edible CBD ban shakes industry
rfi.description: Cannabis use in France is once again under scrutiny, with a drugs monitor reporting a sharp rise in adulterated products on the illegal market, and risky new products entering the legal CBD market. To address the issue of mislabelled products, France has banned edible CBD products, raising concerns in the cannabis industry.

rfi.title: Ebola outbreak spreads in DRC as misinformation hampers response
rfi.description: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have launched an online campaign to tackle growing mistrust surrounding a deadly Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) says misinformation is hampering efforts to contain the haemorrhagic fever, which broke out in the eastern province of Ituri on 15 May.

rfi.title: Mexico brush past ill-disciplined South Africa to launch World Cup party

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

lemonde.title: 39 °C à Paris, plus de 40 °C dans le Sud : la France face à un nouvel épisode de chaleur « très intense et étendu »

france24fr.description: Aonishiki Arata est l’attraction du Tournoi de Sumo de Paris ce week-end à l’Accor Arena. De l’exil hors d’Europe au sumo, le colosse ukrainien s’est installé au Japon depuis seulement quatre ans. Son incroyable destin l’emmène parmi les cinq meilleurs rikishis du monde.

france24fr.title: Iran-Israël : la "guerre des 12 jours" de juin 2025, le début d'une guerre ouverte
france24fr.description: Il y a un an, en juin 2025, Israël et l'Iran s'étaient livré une guerre de 12 jours, déclenchée par une attaque sans précédent d'Israël ayant visé en premier lieu le commandement militaire iranien ainsi que des installations du programme nucléaire. Était-il possible d’imaginer que cette guerre prendrait une telle envergure en 2026 ? Décryptage avec Adel Bakawan, directeur de l’Institut européen d’études sur le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique du Nord.

france24fr.title: Iran : Bertrand Badie raconte comment son père a quitté la Perse à 18 ans
france24fr.description: Toutes les semaines, Judith Grimaldi reçoit un invité dans son émission "Avec Judith". Cette fois-ci, c'est Bertrand Badie, spécialiste des relations internationales. À son micro, il évoque son histoire familiale : sa mère était française et son père, Perse, a quitté son pays en 1928. Aujourd'hui, cet expert reconnu est fier de sa double culture, qu'il qualifie de "richesse extraordinaire".

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : Premier point historique pour le Canada
france24fr.description: Le Canada a décroché un résultat symbolique pour lancer sa Coupe du monde à domicile, en partageant les points avec la Bosnie-Herzégovine (1-1). Jovo Lukic a ouvert le score pour les Bosniens à la 21e minute. Soutenus par leur public à Toronto, les Canadiens ont longtemps poussé avant d’égaliser grâce à Cyle Larin à la 79e minute.

france24fr.title: En Irlande du Nord, des violences anti-immigrés dans une province marquée par les divisions
france24fr.description: Les émeutes anti-immigrés qui ont éclaté lundi dernier à Belfast, en Irlande du Nord, s'inscrivent dans une histoire de conflit et de divisions dans cette province britannique marquée par trois décennies de "troubles", soulignent des habitants et chercheurs interrogés par l'AFP.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Pérou : le candidat de gauche, Roberto Sánchez, propose un recomptage des votes
france24fr.description: Le candidat de gauche Roberto Sánchez a proposé vendredi à sa rivale de droite Keiko Fujimori de réclamer ensemble de recompter tous les bulletins du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Pérou, où ils sont au coude-à-coude, mais le camp de cette dernière a décliné l'offre.

france24fr.title: Élections générales en Guinée : plusieurs partis politiques rejettent les résultats provisoires
france24fr.description: En Guinée, plusieurs partis politiques rejettent les résultats provisoires du double scrutin législatif et communal du 31 mai dernier. Ces formations politiques face à la presse ce matin, dénoncent de nombreuses irrégularités et accusent les autorités électorales d’avoir favorisé la mouvance présidentielle. Des résultats provisoires qui donne le mouvement du Président Mamadi Doumbouya largement victorieux.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : Fayulu et Sesanga blessés après un sit-in contre la réforme constitutionnelle
france24fr.description: La tension monte en République démocratique du Congo. Plusieurs opposants ont été blessés à Kinshasa lors d'une manifestation contre le projet de réforme constitutionnelle porté par la majorité présidentielle. L'opposition accuse le président Félix Tshisekedi de vouloir ouvrir la voie à un troisième mandat malgré les dispositions actuelles de la Constitution. Les précisions avec notre correspondante à Kinshasa, Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Attaques de colons en Cisjordanie occupée : les agriculteurs palestiniens ciblés
france24fr.description: Depuis les attentats du 7 octobre 2023, les violences des colons contre les Palestiniens en Cisjordanie ont fortement augmenté. L'ONU a recensé six attaques en moyenne par jour ces derniers mois. Les éleveurs et les agriculteurs sont les principales victimes.

france24fr.title: Mort de trois marins indiens lors d'attaques américaines sur des navires au large d'Oman
france24fr.description: L'Inde a convoqué vendredi un haut diplomate américain pour la deuxième fois en deux jours, après que des frappes américaines contre trois navires marchands battant pavillon palauien au large d'Oman ont causé la mort de trois Indiens.

france24fr.title: En meeting à Aubervilliers, Raphaël Glucksmann au défi de convaincre son camp
france24fr.description: Raphaël Glucksmann, potentiel candidat à l'élection présidentielle, joue gros pour son meeting samedi à Aubervilliers. Une semaine après le premier meeting du chef de LFI, Jean-Luc Mélenchon – d'ores et déjà candidat – à Saint-Denis, le dirigeant de Place publique, sous pression, s'est donné pour objectif de rallier le Parti socialiste et d'enclencher une dynamique autour de lui.

france24fr.title: Haïti-Ecosse au Mondial 2026 : les Haïtiens veulent croire au rêve
france24fr.description: La qualification pour la Coupe du monde de Haïti se qualifie pour la première fois, depuis un demi-siècle, à la Coupe du monde. Ce pays des Caraïbes, en proie au chaos, veut marquer les esprits pour leur premier match, face à l'Ecosse.

france24fr.title: Iran : "Donald Trump a profondément humilié le peuple persan" (Bertrand Badie)
france24fr.description: Donald Trump "a profondément humilié le peuple persan en disant : 'En une nuit, je vais détruire tout ce que vous êtes'", déplore Bertrand Badie, spécialiste des relations internationales, faisant référence à un message publié par le président américain sur son réseau social Truth Social au mois de mai.L'émission est à retrouver dans son intégralité ce samedi midi sur le site de France 24.

france24fr.title: Cuba annonce un élargissement des activités autorisées pour les entreprises privées

france24fr.title: SpaceX à Wall Street : l'action de l'entreprise d'Elon Musk a pris 19% à son entrée en bourse
france24fr.description: Elon Musk est devenu le premier “trillionnaire” au monde après que les actions de sa société de fusées SpaceX ont grimpé en flèche lors de la plus importante introduction en bourse jamais réalisée à Wall Street. Les actions de SpaceX ont bondi de plus de 19 % après leur mise en cotation vendredi midi, signe que les investisseurs ne se laissent pas décourager par les milliards de pertes enregistrées par l'entreprise.

observador.description: Portugal cumpre primeiro treino em Miami após uma longa viagem de Portugal aos EUA com portas abertas a centenas de pessoas. Ainda, vamos ter jogaço no duelo entre Brasil-Marrocos?

observador.title: Fernando Pimenta conquistou medalha de bronze nos Europeus
observador.description: Atleta liderou boa parte da regata, mas terminou-a atrás de Uladzislau Kravets e Balint Kopasz. Este é o 182.º pódio de Fernando Pimenta, que ainda este sábado disputa a final de K1 500 metros.

observador.title: SpaceX "é única" mas "muitas coisas têm de correr bem"
observador.description: Conhecido como "o sr. IPO", o professor Jay Ritter admite que ser de Elon Musk pode ter tido impacto na oferta inicial da SpaceX, mas no final o que vai contar é o que fará a empresa futurista.

observador.title: As notícias das 12h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: “A dor muda quem somos”
observador.description: Para o médico paliativista Hugo Sarmento Ribeiro, “é bizarro que dor, geriatria e cuidados paliativos não sejam áreas obrigatórias em todos os cursos de medicina”

observador.title: IA. Governo dos EUA ordena retirada de novo serviço Claude
observador.description: Suspensão ocorreu poucos dias depois da Anthropic ter disponibilizado aos assinantes do serviço Claude o modelo Fable 5. Empresa assumiu antes do lançamento que ferramenta é "demasiado poderosa".

observador.title: Cerca 140 concelhos em perigo máximo de incêndio
observador.description: Cerca 140 concelhos de doze distritos de Portugal continental apresentam hoje perigo máximo de incêndio rural. Distritos de Vila Real, Bragança, Castelo Branco e Leiria entre os mais afetados

observador.title: Festivais de Música. "Público está mais exigente"
observador.description: O público dos festivais de música está mais exigente e os promotores têm mais "dores de cabeça" em garantir rentabilidade e em manter a qualidade.

observador.title: Salário médio só aumenta com aumento de produtivide
observador.description: O salário mínimo e o médio estão cada vez mais próximos, verificando-se um fenómeno de compressão salarial, que poderia ser evitado com um aumento da produtividade.

observador.title: Francisca Nabinho: entre a moda e a filigrana
observador.description: A designer de 26 anos assume a direção criativa na Joalharia do Carmo, lança a primeira coleção de joias, investe no conceito "dos pés à cabeça" e diz ser possível viver de moda de autor em Portugal.

observador.title: "Nuclear é questão, mas acordo está próximo"
observador.description: Madalena Mayer Resende admite que Irão e EUA podem estar perto de fechar um entendimento claro. Sublinha, no entanto, a questão nuclear ainda pendente.

observador.title: Nome de Donald Trump começa a ser removido do Kennedy Center
observador.description: Tribunal tinha ordenado a retirada do nome do atual Presidente e centro cultural pediu a prorrogação do prazo para a realização dos trabalhos, que já terão ficado concluídos este sábado.

observador.title: 11h. Época balnear abre com escassez de nadadores salvadores
observador.description: O presidente da Federação Portuguesa de Nadadores Salvadores confessa-se preocupado com a escassez de nadadores salvadores. Ainda,140 concelhos estão em perigo máximo de incêndio.

observador.title: Infarmed retira do mercado produtos cosméticos FBeauty
observador.description: Autoridade do medicamento concluiu que não foram salvaguardadas as "boas práticas de fabrico, avaliação de segurança, ficheiro de informação sobre os produtos e rotulagem".

observador.title: A “febre” Ronaldo contagia Palm Beach
observador.description: A seleção portuguesa chegou ao hotel com um forte apoio de adeptos portugueses, americanos e até dos "adversários" colombianos. Ronaldo foi o mais solicitado, mas ninguém conseguiu ver os jogadores.

spiegel.title: MDR-Intendant Ralf Ludwig: »Wir machen kein Programm für Rechtsextreme«
spiegel.description: Bei einem Wahlsieg der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt könnte zum ersten Mal ein Bundesland aus einer ARD-Anstalt aussteigen. Wie geht der Intendant des Mitteldeutschen Rundfunks, Ralf Ludwig, damit um?

spiegel.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: SPD nominiert Manuela Schwesig erneut zur Spitzenkandidatin
spiegel.description: Beim Parteitag in Wismar erzielt Manuela Schwesig ein Traumergebnis. Die amtierende Ministerpräsidentin sieht ihr Land bei der Landtagswahl vor einer »Richtungsentscheidung«.

spiegel.title: Sydney: Frau bei Hai-Angriff lebensgefährlich verletzt
spiegel.description: Entsetzen in Sydney: Erneut hat ein Hai an einem Strand eine Schwimmerin attackiert. Ein Augenzeuge berichtet von einem erschütternden Schrei.

spiegel.title: Schach: Russland dominierte den Sport über Jahrzehnte. Jetzt bröckelt das System
spiegel.description: Für Russland ist Schach ein Werkzeug für Propaganda und politischen Einfluss. Doch die Machtstrukturen reißen ein. Der Weltverband hat Russland nun gesperrt. Welchen Einfluss hat die Entscheidung? Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Tipps bei Schlafmangel: Was schlaflose Nächte mit Eltern machen - und wie sie sie gut überstehen
spiegel.description: Müde, müder, Eltern: Schlafmedizinerin Sandra Nischwitz weiß, was Schlafentzug mit Müttern und Vätern macht, wie sie trotzdem durch den Tag kommen – und wer sich Hilfe holen sollte.

spiegel.title: Gewaltkriminalität in Deutschland: Straftaten gegen Obdachlose stark gestiegen
spiegel.description: In Deutschland werden wohnungslose Menschen verstärkt Opfer von Straftaten. Ein Bundesland ist besonders betroffen.

spiegel.title: Ostsee: Schwedische Armee fängt zwei russische Kampfjets ab
spiegel.description: Es ist eine bekannte Provokation: Russland hat Kampfjets in die Nähe des schwedischen Luftraums fliegen lassen. Daraufhin starteten auch Kampfflugzeuge der Nato.

spiegel.title: Pride-Parade in Seoul: Zehntausende feiern – ebenso viele protestieren auf Gegendemo
spiegel.description: Zehntausende Menschen feiern ausgelassen bei Südkoreas größter Pride-Parade und fordern mehr Rechte für Lesben, Schwule und trans Personen. Christlich-konservative Gruppen protestieren dagegen.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: USA: Trump-Regierung muss entfernte Tafeln zur Sklaverei vorerst wieder anbringen
spiegel.description: Sklaverei, Rassismus, Diskriminierung – Donald Trump ließ Hinweise auf dunkle Kapitel der US-Geschichte entfernen. Nun stoppte eine Richterin das Vorgehen. Geschichte dürfe nicht »mit einem Korrekturstift« umgeschrieben werden.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Können die USA Sommermärchen?
spiegel.description: Kaum Fans in Washington, in San Diego begeistert alles außer Fußball: ein doppeltes Public-Viewing, an der Ost- und an der Westküste.

spiegel.title: Wie wir mit künstlicher Intelligenz zu einer Gesellschaft der Trickser und Hütchenspieler werden
spiegel.description: Künstliche Intelligenz macht es kinderleicht, sich mit Gedanken zu schmücken, die nicht die eigenen sind. Was macht es mit uns, wenn Täuschung zur Normalität wird?

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Abwehr von Bosniens Sead Kolašinac gegen Kanada - »Absolut sensationell«
spiegel.description: Dem Ex-Schalker Sead Kolašinac ist eine Rettungstat gelungen, die TV-Experte Mats Hummels ins Schwärmen bringt. Und: Die englische Mannschaft wurde offenbar beklaut. Alles Wichtige zur WM im News-Update.

spiegel.title: Israel attackiert Hisbollah im Libanon mit Luftschlägen
spiegel.description: Iran und die USA verhandeln über eine Waffenruhe in Nahost. Die Lage im Libanon ist dabei ein zentraler Punkt. Nun soll die Hisbollah Israel mit Drohnen attackiert haben, das israelische Militär antwortet seinerseits mit Luftangriffen.

spiegel.title: Pflege-Missbrauch: »Da lassen sich Leute die Urlaubsreise finanzieren, samt Ferienwohnung«
spiegel.description: Die Firma von Josef Deutskens hilft Senioren im Alltag. Hier berichtet er, warum die Pflegeversicherung genauer prüfen müsste, wer wirklich Hilfe benötigt – und wie das Solidarsystem in der Praxis missbraucht und ausgenutzt wird.

spiegel.title: Arbeitsmarkt: Deutschland drohen bis 2036 rund 4,3 Millionen fehlende Arbeitskräfte
spiegel.description: Bereits jetzt suchen viele Unternehmen händeringend nach Fachkräften. In Zukunft dürfte sich die Lage verschärfen, weil die Bevölkerung schrumpft, warnt das arbeitgebernahe Instituts der deutschen Wirtschaft.

spiegel.title: Dünger-Ersatz: Vom Trockenklo auf den Acker – und zurück
spiegel.description: Die Straße von Hormus ist blockiert, dadurch wird Dünger immer teurer. Brandenburger »Humuswirte« produzieren Ersatz – aus dem Inhalt von Kompostklos. Wie das funktioniert und was einem großen Geschäft im Wege steht.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: USA gewinnen Auftaktspiel gegen Paraguay im eigenen Land
spiegel.description: Das erste WM-Spiel der amerikanischen Mannschaft endet mit einem perfekten Ergebnis für den Gastgeber. In einem perfekten Stadion. Mit perfekter Organisation. Nur die Emotionen der Zuschauer bleiben seltsam stumpf.

elpais.description: El país vota este domingo si fija un tope de 10 millones a la población. Una localidad pequeña que conserva el sabor rural y una del área metropolitana de Zúrich que levanta rascacielos exponen el dilema que plantea el referéndum

elpais.title: Delphine Horvilleur, rabina: “Los judíos han aprendido de la historia que nunca encontrarán la paz”
elpais.description: Es una de las pocas rabinas frases. Sobre el judaísmo ha escrito libros como ‘Reflexiones sobre la cuestión antisemita’ o ‘Comprender el mundo’. Y sobre la muerte y el duelo, ‘Vivir con nuestros muertos’ o su nuevo obra, ‘Cómo hablar de la muerte a los niños’. Crítica acerada de Benjamín Netanyahu, vive amenazada por quienes desconfían de su sionismo y por los que confunden la reivindicación de un territorio protegido con una postura política nacionalista y belicista

elpais.title: Arriortúa, el guerrero en jefe que cambió las reglas de la industria de automoción mundial
elpais.description: El ejecutivo vasco, conocido como ‘Superlópez’ en sus años de mayor actividad, originó un enfrentamiento histórico entre General Motors y Volkswagen

elpais.title: John Connolly, una mirada empática al lado más oscuro: “Es importante no ser cómplices del mal”
elpais.description: El creador de la serie del detective Charlie Parker reflexiona sobre su proceso creativo, sus miedos y anhelos y anticipa un final para su héroe

nyt.title: Wages Are Falling. Wealth Is Surging. No Wonder Americans Are Unhappy.

nyt.title: Mega I.P.O. Frenzy Could Be a Harbinger of a Stock Bubble

nyt.title: Despite US Help, Little Oil Has Gone Through Strait of Hormuz

nyt.title: What to Know About the Ebola Outbreak

npr.title: Pope Leo XIV's flight home from Spain was grounded so the king came to his aid

npr.title: Trump says U.S. military strike killed leader of Tren de Aragua gang

npr.title: She waited decades for Scotland to make the World Cup. At 93, she'll cheer in person
npr.description: Moira Brown, perhaps the oldest of Scotland's Tartan Army of soccer fans, will be in Boston when Scotland's team plays against Haiti on June 13. "I'm the luckiest person in this world," she says.

npr.title: Ousted South Korean President Yoon given prison term for drone flights over Pyongyang

npr.title: The Teddy Bear Doctor treats stuffies in need of care

npr.title: U.S. and Iran peace deal within reach, Pakistan's prime minister says

phys-org.title: Lab-grown canine muscle cells offer solution for early therapeutic testing

phys-org.description: By integrating findings from 140 studies and nearly 66,000 individuals, researchers from the Biosocial team at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development in collaboration with Columbia University in New York have shown that lower socioeconomic status and exposure to discrimination are consistently associated with accelerated biological aging, measured in the epigenome.

phys-org.description: Pomacea canaliculata, commonly known as the apple snail, is a pest commonly found in Hong Kong's wetlands and farmlands. It is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) among 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species.

phys-org.title: Scientist creates 'mini‑universe' to measure time without a clock
phys-org.description: A University of Birmingham scientist has built a "mini-universe" that takes a step toward answering one of science's biggest questions: "What is time?" Publishing his findings in Physical Review Research, Professor Giovanni Barontini shows how it is possible to measure the flow of time without using a clock at all. The new findings provide a scientific model in which a version of time emerges from the experiment itself.

phys-org.title: Trees may store less carbon than expected in the future

From biomedical sensors to self-powered infrastructure monitoring sensors, mechanoluminescent materials have a wide range of potential applications. However, high-performance mechanoluminescent materials have traditionally relied on expensive rare-earth materials or complex material compositions.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime

Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

proj-syn.description: The G7 summit must recognize that extreme disparities in income, wealth, opportunity, and political influence are not only a defining feature of the global economy but also a major factor in many other shared challenges. proj-syn.title: Modi Is Rigging Indian Democracy

proj-syn.title: Learning to Govern a Fragmented World

The upcoming G7 summit offers a unique opportunity to champion a coalition-based approach that translates shared interests into collective action.

proj-syn.title: Cognition for Sale
proj-syn.description: AI is doing what no previous technology could, turning tacit human knowledge into a product that can be extracted, priced, and distributed at scale. Yet the same technology that democratizes cognitive labor may also weaken the human capacities on which complex societies depend.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech Gets Bigger
proj-syn.description: Recent stock-market gyrations are a reminder of just how dependent the United States and global economies have become on investors’ seemingly insatiable appetite for tech stocks. Even if a major correction is in the offing, however, it will not happen before SpaceX’s massive initial public offering draws in yet more leveraged investment, nor will it destroy the market power of the other tech giants that have spent years perfecting anti-competitive tactics that largely escape regulators’ purvi

proj-syn.title: The Democrats Need a Story, Not More Lists
proj-syn.description: Whereas Donald Trump has offered voters a clear and compelling narrative, Democrats have provided only vague aspirations and long lists of policies. To win over voters—rather than scrounging protest votes—they must articulate a compelling economic vision, with wage-led growth as its foundation.

proj-syn.title: What if Europe Loses Access to Its Climate Data?
proj-syn.description: The European Green Deal runs on data, from corporate disclosures to climate-risk analyses and decarbonization pathways. But much of this data feeds platforms and tools developed outside the European Union, which could threaten the bloc’s climate agenda and even its foundational values.

proj-syn.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
proj-syn.description: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

proj-syn.title: Peak Oil Demand Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: Amid the disruptions caused by the US/Israeli-Iran war, countries have begun adapting to life with less oil. What started as a supply shock has become a demand story, forcing the energy sector to reconsider one of its most important assumptions: continued growth of global oil demand.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.
